summary: This standards-track RFC defines a way to clone an IKEv2 security association, for cases where a VPN user has several interfaces or the gateway is a cluster of nodes with different addresses. A new tunnel can be set up quickly from an existing one without a full new negotiation.

plainLanguage.summary: Instead of proving who you are again for each new door, you copy your pass so each door can accept you.

questions: how to clone an ikev2 sa
subtitle: Spawn extra IKEv2 tunnels from one authenticated session, with no second login.

tldr.problem: Every IKEv2 IKE SA normally needs its own authentication, which can take several round trips, user activity and crypto work. That is costly when a peer has several interfaces or a gateway cluster has several nodes.
tldr.mechanism: Peers announce support with a CLONE_IKE_SA_SUPPORTED notification in IKE_AUTH. Later, one peer sends a CREATE_CHILD_SA that looks like an IKE SA rekey plus a CLONE_IKE_SA notification, so the old IKE SA is kept and a second one appears.
tldr.outcome: The new IKE SA is created without the authentication exchange and can later be moved with MOBIKE or assigned to another cluster node. The cost is that accounting and limits based on one IKE SA per authentication can be sidestepped.

today: RFC 7791 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 7296 and is meant to be combined with MOBIKE (RFC 4555).

sections.title: Why Clone an IKE SA
sections.content:
The main scenario is a VPN end user connecting to a Security Gateway when at least one side has multiple interfaces. With n = 2 interfaces on one side this means up to 2 VPNs, and with 2 interfaces on each side up to m x n VPNs.

With plain IKEv2 (RFC 7296), each VPN needs its own IKE SA, and each IKE SA needs authentication. Authentication might need multiple round trips and activity from the end user (as with EAP-SIM or EAP-TLS), plus crypto operations that add delay.

A second scenario is load balancing. Copying IKE and IPsec state to every cluster node requires anti-replay data such as the sequence number to be synchronized for every outgoing AH or ESP packet, which makes high-speed systems hard to build. Moving a client with the Redirect Mechanism (RFC 5685) forces a new IKE SA from scratch, and Session Resumption (RFC 5723) needs the client to know the new gateway beforehand.
sections.plainLanguage: If you have two phones, you do not want to show your ID again for each one. Cloning lets the second one borrow the trust the first one already earned.

sections.title: Protocol Overview
sections.content:
The peers first agree that they can clone, by exchanging CLONE_IKE_SA_SUPPORTED notifications during IKE_AUTH. To create a new parallel IKE SA, one peer starts a CREATE_CHILD_SA exchange as if it were rekeying the existing IKE SA, and adds a CLONE_IKE_SA notification.

In a normal rekey, the old IKE SA is deleted once the rekey succeeds (Section 2.8 of RFC 7296). The CLONE_IKE_SA notification says the current IKE SA must not be deleted, so two IKE SAs coexist.

The RFC says that deciding which extra VPNs to create and when is up to the host's local policy, and that with multiple interfaces on both ends care should be taken to avoid VPNs being duplicated by both ends. It also notes that cloning is independent of MOBIKE and could serve other future scenarios.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a normal "get a new key" request with a note attached saying "keep the old one too". You end up with two keys instead of a swap.

sections.title: Negotiating Support
sections.content:
Both sides indicate support by sending CLONE_IKE_SA_SUPPORTED. It MUST be sent in the IKE_AUTH exchange; if there are multiple IKE_AUTH exchanges, the initiator sends it in its first IKE_AUTH message and the responder in its last one.

Only if both sides sent it may the IKE SA be cloned. Otherwise the IKE SA MUST NOT be cloned.
sections.plainLanguage: Both people must say "yes, I can do copies" while checking in. If either stays quiet, no copies are allowed.

sections.title: Cloning and Error Handling
sections.content:
The initiator sends a CREATE_CHILD_SA request that rekeys the IKE SA and contains CLONE_IKE_SA. The notification MUST appear only in that request; in any other message it MUST be ignored. The responder rekeys, creates the new IKE SA and keeps the old one, and the response carries no extra Notify payloads.

Unlike a regular rekey, existing Child SAs MUST NOT be transferred to the new IKE SA. Signaling for them keeps going over the old IKE SA.

If the responder cannot clone temporarily (not enough resources, or the IKE SA is being deleted), it SHOULD answer with TEMPORARY_FAILURE, and the initiator MAY retry after a while. If the responder limits how many IKE SAs one peer may have, it SHOULD answer NO_ADDITIONAL_SAS. That is permanent, and the initiator SHOULD NOT retry until some existing SAs with the responder are deleted.
sections.plainLanguage: The new copy starts empty, and old rooms stay with the old key. If the guard is busy, try later. If the guard says you have too many copies, wait until you hand some back.

sections.title: The Notify Payloads
sections.content:
Both notifications use the Notify payload format from Section 3.10 of RFC 7296. This document sets Protocol ID to zero and SPI Size to zero. The Notify Message Type (2 octets) is 16432 for CLONE_IKE_SA_SUPPORTED and 16433 for CLONE_IKE_SA.

IANA allocated these two values in the "IKEv2 Notify Message Types - Status Types" registry.
sections.plainLanguage: Each note is a small standard form with two special numbers: one for "I can copy" and one for "please copy now".

sections.title: Example: One User, Two Interfaces
sections.content:
Appendix A is informational and shows a VPN end user with two interfaces building two VPNs without authenticating twice. First VPN_0 is built over Interface_0 with ordinary IKEv2, with both sides advertising MOBIKE and clone support. They may also advertise extra addresses with ADDITIONAL_IP4_ADDRESS or ADDITIONAL_IP6_ADDRESS.

Next the user clones the IKE SA, then creates a Child SA for VPN_1 on the new IKE SA. At this point both VPNs still use Interface_0, and the RFC leaves it out of scope how the end user handles traffic with multiple interfaces, for example overlapping Traffic Selectors. Finally MOBIKE moves VPN_1 to Interface_1.
sections.plainLanguage: You sign in once on your laptop's Wi-Fi, make a copy of your pass, then slide the copy over to the cable connection.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The protocol does not modify IKEv2, and security considerations are mostly those of RFC 7296. But cloning lets an initiator duplicate existing SAs, which may affect accounting or control based on a single IKE SA per authentication.

A limit on the number of IKE SAs could be exhausted by one user. A limit on Child SAs per IKE SA could be overstepped, so such a system should count Child SAs over all IKE SAs of an end user. Monitoring based on the first IKE SA's lifetime could miss use continuing on a clone, so service use should be counted from the first IKE SA's start until the last is removed. Implementations can always limit the number of cloned IKE SAs.

When used for load balancing, IKE SA state with session keys must be transferred between nodes, so implementations must take due precautions. How that is done is out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: Copies of a pass make it harder to count how many people are inside, so the guard needs to count all copies together.

messages.label: CREATE_CHILD_SA: N(CLONE_IKE_SA), SA, Ni, KEi
messages.note: Looks like an IKE SA rekey; the old IKE SA is kept.
